runs.t: Webhooks deliver events via outbound HTTP calls; message queues broker asynchronous delivery between producers and consumers. Both decouple work in time but have different trust and operational models.

Design retries, deduplication, signatures, replay protection, dead-letter handling and schema evolution. Do not assume delivery order or exactly-once effects unless the specific system guarantees them end-to-end.
A payment provider sends a signed charge-success webhook. The receiver verifies authenticity, stores the event ID, acknowledges quickly and processes the state change asynchronously once.
Webhook endpoints are exposed to forged requests, slow handlers and SSRF-like delivery misconfiguration. Queue consumers can poison the queue without retry limits and dead-letter visibility.
